title: Scars: how your baggage shapes decisions and how to guard against its blind spots
summary: Jason Cohen argues that our emotional baggage defines who we are but also creates blind spots. Using a hosting-cost example from WP Engine, he shows how bootstrapper habits can misallocate time once a company is funded. His fix: define core values, build a company that fits them, and seek compatible outside counsel.

principles.text: Bootstrapped habits (grab cash now) become wrong once you have money in the bank; invest time in growth instead.
principles.quote: If you're bootstrapping, getting that $1000/mo *right now* is the better choice. Money is scarce, time is precious, and $1000 today is better than $5000 next year (which you might not survive to see).

principles.text: A good hourly-rate argument can still hide a worse use of time; compare against growth investments.
principles.quote: I could have used those 10 hours to make it easier to share a website speed report, and that might have resulted in 1000 people trying it over the next year

principles.text: With money in the bank, the point of investment is to turn money today into a growing, predictable revenue machine.
principles.quote: The whole point of an investment is to turn "money today" into long-term value, meaning a growing, profitable, predictable revenue machine.

principles.text: Define core values you'd hold even at the cost of money, fame or relationships; they also form company culture.
principles.quote: First, you have to decide what your core beliefs are: The inalienable tenets by which you want to live your life, no matter what--even if it means making less money, or increasing risk

principles.text: Build a company where the natural, consistent decisions match your temperament and values.
principles.quote: Decide to build a company in which the correct, consistent decisions are the ones you'll naturally take.

principles.text: You can't see your own blind spots; surround yourself with honest trusted advisors and actually listen.
principles.quote: Escape the echo chamber of your own head. Because, as in the example above, you **cannot know you're wrong**.
